source_snapshot.procedure: Inventory NVMe, download firmware to /dev/nvme0, commit slot 1 action 3, deliberately power-cycle during flashing, reboot and check NVMe information.
source_snapshot.criteria: After interrupted flash, NVMe still works normally; no measurable identity, firmware, health, namespace or I/O definition.
source_snapshot.script: No Script; Config-Check; 20/20 minutes; unique code/variant.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL and substitutes corrupted/wrong-image rejection for the source-required timed power interruption.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/CRITICAL; preserves interruption and requires disposable target, vendor timing, controlled power/console and recovery.

old_problem: The source intentionally removes power during firmware commit but does not restrict the target to disposable non-boot media, define vendor-supported interruption timing, prove slot/action semantics, provide recovery, or define normal operation. DeepSeek changes the stimulus to corrupt-image rejection, which tests a different failure mode.
disposition_reason: The original negative coverage is retained: corrupt-image rejection cannot replace loss of power during commit. ED-07 and ED-18 require separate flash and complete OFF-to-ON authorization/evidence; ED-11/12 prohibit autonomous execution and retry. The review is resolvable as a package-gated destructive test on an immutable-identity disposable drive, conditional on vendor interruption guidance and a proven recovery/RMA path. Only authoritative SPEC may make it N/A.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2042, same-row DeepSeek, GPT V2, historical record, unique-code result and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next row Functionality 2043 / Wistron-BIOS-00492-V002 / bb025c27de5c43b5 was directly read from XLSX.
Wrong/corrupt-image rejection validates image validation, whereas power loss during an accepted commit validates atomicity or recovery; these are distinct and cannot share a verdict.
The target must be disposable, non-boot, unmounted, data-free and bound by model/serial/PCI identity because interruption may permanently remove the controller.
Slot 1/action 3, the observable commit phase, cut timing and recovery behavior are accepted only from the exact model's vendor documentation.
PASS needs full OFF-to-ON-to-OS-ready evidence plus controller identity, revision/slot, namespaces, SMART/error logs and approved I/O health; `nvme list` alone is insufficient.
No nvme command, image access/write, commit, power interruption/cycle, recovery, I/O or DUT action was performed.

test_case.test_name: Vendor-approved interrupted NVMe firmware commit and post-recovery integrity
test_case.purpose: Verify that the exact disposable M.2 NVMe target remains recoverable and healthy after the vendor-approved firmware-commit phase is intentionally interrupted by a controlled complete power cycle, preserving this stimulus separately from corrupt-image rejection.
required_package: Exact row-2042 variant plus disposable target model/serial/PCI/controller/namespace identity and written boot/mount/RAID/data-free proof
Vendor-approved image/tool/checksum, slot 1/action 3 semantics, supported interruption observable/window and expected atomicity/recovery behavior
Explicit one-run authorizations for firmware download/commit and separately for controlled OFF-to-ON power cycle
Controlled PDU/console/log capture, maintenance isolation, stable restore power and OS-ready definition
Recovery image/media/tool, documented vendor recovery/RMA steps, spare device and human verdict owner
test_case.test_command: DESTRUCTIVE PACKAGE-AND-AUTHORIZATION-GATED; first collect immutable target identity, data/boot/mount/RAID exclusion, pre-revision/slot/namespaces/SMART/error logs and validate image/checksum/compatibility, commit semantics, vendor interruption window and recovery. Obtain separately scoped flash and power-cycle approvals. On the isolated disposable target only, run the approved download and commit while capturing console/PDU/timestamps; cut power only at the documented observable, prove complete OFF, restore ON once, wait for defined OS Ready, then re-identify the controller and collect revision/slot/namespaces/SMART/error logs and approved non-destructive I/O health. Do not substitute corrupt-image rejection or retry any phase.
test_case.expected_result: At the documented interruption point, the platform completes OFF-to-ON-to-OS-ready once; the same disposable controller either retains the prior valid firmware or activates the vendor-defined recoverable revision, enumerates all expected namespaces, has no new critical SMART/error condition and passes the approved non-destructive health check without manual hidden remediation.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires vendor support for the interruption, exact identity and two authorizations, full cut/restore/OS-ready timeline, an allowed revision/slot outcome and complete post-recovery health. FAIL on wrong/in-use target, uncontrolled timing, controller disappearance outside the documented recoverable path, boot failure, unexpected revision/slot, missing namespace, critical health/error or failed I/O. Vendor prohibition may be N/A only with exact SPEC evidence; missing package/recovery/approval is NOT READY.
safety_gate: Disposable non-boot, unmounted, data-free target and documented recovery/RMA/spare are mandatory before download.
Firmware write and complete power cycle require separate explicit authorizations naming target, image and interruption window.
One attempt only; stop on any mismatch, missed timing, unexpected state, controller loss or boot/health failure and preserve evidence.
No automatic retry, extra power cycle, rollback or recovery; any recovery requires a new vendor-approved authorization.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/Variant/hash and proof that corrupt-image rejection is excluded/separate
Disposable target identity plus boot/mount/RAID/data-free proof, vendor compatibility/interruption/recovery documents and image checksum
Separate flash and power-cycle approvals with target/image/window/expiry
Pre-state and full download/commit/console/PDU OFF-to-ON-to-OS-ready timeline
Post-state identity, allowed revision/slot, namespaces, SMART/error logs and non-destructive health result
No-retry audit, any failure preservation, recovery readiness and engineer verdict or SPEC-backed N/A
test_case.recovery: On wrong identity, missed cut window, controller loss, boot failure or health regression, stop and preserve image/command/console/PDU/SMART/SEL evidence. Keep the device and system isolated; do not repeat commit or power cycle. Invoke recovery or RMA only under a new explicit authorization following the exact vendor procedure, then revalidate identity and data isolation before service release.

source_conflict.reason: The source interruption is restored, corrupt-image substitution is explicitly separated, and vendor timing plus disposable-target/recovery rules make the intended negative test unambiguous.

blocked.reason: A complete conditional test and recovery boundary exist; vendor documents, disposable hardware and approvals are runtime package gates. SPEC-backed prohibition yields N/A, not an invented PASS.
